source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
For red corn grown in Kampong Cham and Kandal provinces, the document diagrams the following value-chain flow (Figure 9 in the source):

Producers (farmers): sell either wet cob corn at farm-gate prices of about 600-700 riel/kg, or dried kernel corn at about 600-800 riel/kg.

Corn flows either directly to district-level collectors (who purchase corn in the local market, own their own scales/weighing equipment, negotiate price and volume with farmers, and arrange transport, sometimes financed by advances or ties to particular villages) or via feed-mill factories (including named groups such as Betagro, New Hope, and other feed-mill companies who buy corn as raw material for animal feed).

From the district collectors, corn is then sold on to exporters who ship to Vietnam -- these are buyers based near the Vietnam border who set purchase prices for corn coming from collectors in Kampong Cham and Kandal, and who then re-export to buyers inside Vietnam and to feed-mill and grain-trading networks in Vietnamese border towns.
